title: Garena to premiere first episode of anime spinoff Free Fire: Daybreak at Brazil's CCXP26
summary: With all the news about gaming spinoffs, including PUBG Mobile getting an adaptation helmed by Donald Glover of all people, you'd be forgiven for forgetting about Garena's own Free Fire animated series. But it's just been announced that the first episode of Free Fire: Daybreak will debut at Brazil's CCXP26 convention! The series follows the characters Hayato, Moco and Kelly (the game's mascot) in an adventure set in New Dawn City. Controlled by the Horizon Corporation, there are mysteries afoot and a strange new power that'll aid our intrepid protagonists in breaking free of the constraints of society. ... [MORE]

title: Dungeon Splat! proves that clearing monsters from a dungeon is messy business
summary: If there's one stereotype about fantasy adventurers that's true, it's that they mostly have a 'kill first, ask questions never' policy. Have you ever stopped to wonder if you needed to slaughter that group of Orcs hanging around minding their own business? Me neither. And if violently massacring everything in your path is your thing, then Dungeon Splat is for you! Available now on iOS, Dungeon Splat! pits your intrepid adventurer against a winding dungeon full of enemies. Your job? Simply to clear it out in messy, messy fashion. You simply swipe to send your adventurer hurtling and cleaving through enemies, leaving a spray of comfortably PG neon blood and guts in your wake. ... [MORE]

title: Copy Cats is a cat-cloning platformer where you'll need all the help you can get
summary: Back in the day, most games lived and died based on a gimmick - a mechanic or selling point you could sum up in a sentence. Of course, that's quite reductive, but every now and then something comes along that harkens back to that time, such as Copy Cats, which is available to buy now on iOS and Android! The concept of Copy Cats is simple: you play a cat transported into a virtual wood that needs to make their escape. Fortunately, you'll have virtual clones of yourself to help you out. The only problem? These clones don't have a mind of their own, and you'll be controlling both yourself and them, all at once. ... [MORE]

title: PUBG Mobile to receive its own live-action series starring Donald Glover on Netflix
summary: It would seem that, off the back of the success of shows such as Arcane and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, the folks at Netflix are banking on another big name in gaming to carry them to success. And as it turns out, it's PUBG getting the nod with its own live-action series on the streaming service, now in development! Details are very scarce at the moment, but we know that none other than storied actor Donald Glover of Atlanta and Community fame will be aboard as both executive producer, director, writer and star. Other details, be they plot or other cast members, aren't available, but watch this space for more information. ... [MORE]

title: Batomon Showdown lets you enjoy creature-collecting fun with a roguelike, autobattler twist
summary: As we head towards midday, it seems fitting that we go for something that firmly falls into the middle between two genres in a very interesting way. And that's with Batomon Showdown, the roguelike autobattler that has more than a bit of a similarity to Pokémon about it, available to play right now on iOS and Android! From the creatures to the characters, it's clear that Batomon Showdown is emulating the classic 2D Pokemon games. But rather than offering a throwback to them, as something like Cassette Beasts did, Batomon Showdown instead transforms it into a roguelike autobattler, where synergies and team comp matter more than individual power! ... [MORE]

title: Where Winds Meet teases a chaotic battlefield next month ahead of its 1st anniversary festivities, and you're invited
summary: NetEase Games and Everstone Studio teased a new region two weeks ago, and in case you missed it, Qingzhou is finally here for you to explore. The Wuxia RPG has also just opened the Isle of Penglai yesterday, so I'd say there's a lot to unpack here before the month ends! As for Qingzhou, it's dubbed "the most welcoming region in the Jianghu", largely thanks to the friendly locals who'd gladly lend a hand to lost wanderers in the region. I suppose that extends to how they settle disputes too, because the Sect - Inkbound Order values peaceful resolutions to conflict where the pen is indeed mightier than the sword. ... [MORE]

title: Hearth and Hamlet lets you build your kingdom at your own pace, so no pressure, really
summary: Incremental clickers have never really, well, clicked with me, only because it's the rapid clicking that injured my arms in the first place (curse you, tennis elbows). But Hearth and Hamlet does seem to offer something a tad more mellow than any kind of frantic tapping, as it's supposed to be a more relaxing experience where you build your medieval kingdom from scratch.  This incremental citybuilder will have you gathering resources and constructing buildings across lovely pixel-art visuals, with workers you can assign to make your settlement thrive. Of course, while it's all nice and cosy at the beginning, you're still running a kingdom, so you'll need to manage morale and handle civic decisions too. Plus, there's the omnipresent tax system to navigate - there's no escaping those, even in the virtual world, it seems. ... [MORE]

title: War Robots welcomes Halloween with alien tripods from War of the Worlds
summary: Just in time for Halloween, War Robots' 12.5 update is going full War of the Worlds with its "Halloween Interlopers", because if you're looking for something different this season apart from your average vampires and werewolves, the PvP shooter from My.Games has you covered. It's all about channelling H.G. Wells in this invasion as the in-universe "Evolife Broadcasting Systems" introduces the novel's alien tripods, and with a new theme comes new map features you can duke it out with too. That includes the Tripedal Robot (Nekton) and its extended Absorber shield, plus a new Tactical Drone (Object) that can offer support to flying and Absorber-shielded robots - perfect for pairing with Nekton. ... [MORE]

title: Leafy Corner lets you flex your green thumb and give virtual plants some TLC
summary: I've always wanted to be like those cool herb-savvy cooks who can grow their own produce in the kitchen, but alas, plants have never really taken a liking to me. Leafy Corner at least helps me care for (or at least attempt to care for) digital flora, as it's coming to mobile in 2027. I say 2027 like it's some sort of faraway future, but I just realised upon writing this that that's only two months away, isn't it? Which is definitely a good thing, as Leafy Corner will finally let me try and give plants some TLC in my own virtual shop. title: StarVaders lets you pilot a mech against aliens using replayable decks, and maybe even rewind time too
summary: Deckbuilding roguelikes have always had a special place in my heart, which is why I'm doubly looking forward to StarVaders, Snapbreak Games' upcoming, well, deckbuilding roguelike. The hand-drawn feel of the art style adds to its overall charm in my opinion, and since you get to fend off an alien invasion at that, it's already got my attention from the get-go. Basically, you pilot a cool mech to repel said hostile invaders across a grid-based battlefield, and as you might expect, you'll really need to put your tactical thinking to the test if you want to gain the upper hand. There are all sorts of satisfying combos to chain together to really ramp up the exhilaration of a well-thought-out move. And as it seems like you can even manipulate time to your liking, I feel like the strategic combinations here will be as varied as they can be. ... [MORE]

title: Cages: Hidden Worlds is a puzzling, quirky adventure where you escape a forgotten freak show
summary: It's been a big day for mobile announcements, with the likes of Planet of Lana II and Darkest Dungeon II, among others, all set to make their way to mobile. But there're also a few lesser-known, hidden gems buried amongst the announcements, such as the unnerving little puzzle adventure Cages: Hidden Worlds that's set to launch in 2027. The best way to describe Cages: Hidden Worlds is via my initial impression, which is that this is a point-and-click adventure if it were made by Tim Burton. Set in a mysterious mansion packed with the remains of an abandoned freak show and its imprisoned inhabitants, Cages: Hidden Worlds tasks you with solving complex and esoteric puzzles as you attempt to make your escape. ... [MORE]

title: Planet of Lana II launches in Android Early Access as iOS pre-orders approach
summary: Only a few days ago, the first Planet of Lana was named as one of the ports getting proper iPhone Duo support. Now the sequel has shown up on the radar too. Planet of Lana II: Children of the Leaf is out in Early Access on Android, with iOS pre-orders coming soon. Lana and Mui are back, and their home planet isn’t in great shape. Greed and power have split the tribes of Novo apart, and the pair end up standing against whoever’s reshaping it, with a few truths about Mui’s past surfacing on the way. As before, nobody says a word. It’s all carried by the visuals and an orchestral score. ... [MORE]

title: Everything is Crab mixes Spore and Vampire Survivors for an evolutionary roguelike
summary: Carcinisation is the process by which, entirely independent of one another, multiple species all evolve into a crablike form. So, for a game about evolution, it should be no surprise that Everything is Crab takes a pretty loose approach to the concept. And now, this mashup of Spore and Vampire Survivors is coming to mobile November 24th! Everything is Crab sees you take on the role of Darwin, an amorphous, featureless blue blob who eats other creatures in order to gain evolutionary traits. As he becomes more evolved, he gains new abilities and can become everything from a friendly herbivore to a carnivorous apex predator! ... [MORE]
